title: fs: close file streams with fd 0
body:
The shared close helper in `lib/internal/fs/streams.js` uses `if (!stream.fd)` to skip cleanup when no descriptor is available. This also matches fd `0`, which is a valid file descriptor. As a result, a stream can emit `'close'` while the underlying descriptor remains open.

```diff
-  if (!stream.fd) {
+  if (stream.fd == null) {
```

Check for `null` or `undefined` instead, so fd `0` follows the same close path as other descriptors. This also allows the optional flush handling and clearing of `stream.fd` to run.

Add regression coverage for both `ReadStream` and `WriteStream` using the existing `options.fs` override. The test verifies that the supplied `close` implementation is called exactly once with fd `0`. It fails with the original guard and does not close the test process's actual stdin.

For file-backed `process.stdin`, `autoClose: false` continues to preserve the descriptor at EOF, while an explicit `destroy()` now closes fd `0`. Actual descriptor closure, stdin EOF behavior, and snapshot build/restore were verified locally.

Fixes: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/57905
